title: Toward Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence for Users’ Digital Well-Being: Systematic Review, Synthesis, and Future Directions
preview: Literature review synthesizing human-centered AI approaches to digital well-being and future system design.

title: How AI-Driven Search May Reshape Democracy, Economics, and Human Agency
preview: Analytical essay examining AI search interfaces, independent verification and users' control over information discovery.

title: Generative AI tool use enhances academic achievement in sustainable education through shared metacognition and cognitive offloading among preservice teachers
preview: Examines cognitive offloading and metacognition in AI-supported education; attention fragmentation is not a direct reported outcome.

title: "It makes you think": Provocations Help Restore Critical Thinking to AI-Assisted Knowledge Work
preview: Study of 24 participants examining provocations such as critiques and alternatives alongside AI suggestions as supports for reflection.

title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Confidence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers
preview: Survey of 319 knowledge workers investigating generative AI and self-reported critical thinking and cognitive effort; does not establish AI-caused attention fragmentation.

title: The Battle for Cognitive Liberty in the Age of Corporate AI
preview: Commentary about cognitive autonomy, AI systems, and the monetization of attention; an argument rather than evidence of measured cognitive effects.

title: Attention hijacked: How social media notifications disrupt cognitive processing
preview: Experimental research on notifications and cognitive-task disruption; adjacent digital attention evidence, not direct AI exposure.

title: Intelligent support for digital wellbeing: A design framework through a systematic literature review
preview: Systematic review proposing a design framework for intelligent digital well-being systems.

title: Attention is all they need: cognitive science and the (techno)political economy of attention in humans and machines
preview: Conceptual analysis connecting AI-optimized engagement, cognition, attention economics and well-being.

title: Batching smartphone notifications can improve well-being
preview: Randomized field experiment of 237 people comparing notification schedules and well-being, not an AI-specific intervention.

title: The Paradox of AI Assistance: Better Results, Worse Thinking
preview: Higher-education commentary considering reduced cognitive effort, trust, and overreliance in AI-assisted work.

title: The cost of interrupted work: More speed and stress
preview: Foundational experimental study of interrupted work, time pressure and stress. Relevant as adjacent evidence.

title: Beyond the attention economy, towards an ecology of attending. A manifesto
preview: Philosophical argument for attention as embedded in sociotechnical systems and human well-being.
